evidence: The three named inputs exist: instruction.md:7,9 names /instructions/hireops_rules.md, /instructions/integration.md and /assets/seed_data.json; environment/Dockerfile:14-16 copies and makes both directories readable. Agent build log records both COPY steps and image sha256:6f870f89caf1f289e70732cbc1d5a430722288d7902f0dc56f58728da69b0e84. Independently rehashed input-binding.json as b0d475a9cf64ed2e01b6a01999e8baa1302e27f6f74b9b95faf00d5490312fbb, matching the current evidence index; its actual image file hashes match all three frozen inputs. The public and golden seeds are byte-identical (SHA256 1b39015461a7a4f23b835aeea9584caffd0266c64d394778376cbd6c8a18bcf7). db.js:14-20,122-179 consumes that local seed; solve.sh:33 deploys it, consistent with instruction.md:13 runtime asset-copy requirement. Parsed the judge P0 JSON and compared its semantic projection against the public seed: 7 requisitions, 13 offers, 3 employees, 8 commitments, 1 grant, 2 signing payments and 2 referral accruals all match after resolving actor/referrer IDs to their public names and deriving the stated referral split. Reference clock, rates and thresholds agree with the rules and app_context. A divergent golden-only fixture could falsely validate an app, but byte identity rules out that asset counterexample here. A conforming alternative with different financial row IDs/schema/order or dollar/date presentation remains allowed by P0 and judge.toml:65,74,83,92. This is asset/content evidence only, not a configured judge or portal result.
